## Posts: the stage totals and the four writers (`FluxRegister`) {#sec-ch10-posts}

### Summary

A stage's face fluxes live in the register as one total per active direction. The producers write those totals
directly, and every later change goes through one of four writers: `add`, `scale`, `replace` and the private
`overwrite_`. Only `overwrite_` books anything, and it books exactly what it changed. Every writer marks its
direction as written, which the prescribed faces of @sec-ch10-prescribed read.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Hold the stage totals $T_d$ and the kept parts, and change them only through writers that keep the order and book the overwrites, @eq-ch10-overwrite.

**Data.** In: the producers' face fluxes, $(n_{\mathrm{var}}, n_3, n_2, n_1)$ per direction, in the flux dtype. Out: the same tensors, changed in place; booked rates to the monitor.

**Placement.** Every stage, inside `HydroImpl::forward` and `ScalarImpl::forward`.

**Activation.** Always; a direction with one cell has no total.

**Guarantee / limits.** Adds happen in call order and are never fused; an overwrite books $\sum_f A_f\,(\text{after}-\text{before})$ per row.

**Evidence.** `test_flux_register.<b>` (Tests).
:::

Local symbols: $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ is the direction, $T_d$ its stage total, $f$ a face of $T_d$, $A_f$ its area and
$r$[^rg-0cf14ab9beae] a row of the total.

### Derivation

None: the register discretises nothing. The one formula it implements is the booking of an overwrite. When a writer
replaces the values of a set of faces $\mathcal F$ of $T_d$, the change of the face-integrated transfer of row $r$
is

$$
a_r = \sum_{f\in\mathcal F} A_f\,\bigl(T_{d,r,f}^{\text{after}} - T_{d,r,f}^{\text{before}}\bigr),
$$ {#eq-ch10-overwrite}

a rate (per unit time, at the step's $\Delta t$[^rg-e08a4caa8890], before the stage weights) that the monitor turns into a step amount
(@sec-ch10-amounts). Faces outside $\mathcal F$ contribute nothing, because there the difference is zero.

### Numerical method

**The totals.** `reset` allocates one zero total per active direction, shaped $(n_{\mathrm{var}}, n_3, n_2, n_1)$ in
the flux dtype, and a direction with one cell has none ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::reset overload=1 >}}).
The hydro module resets its register with the coordinate, so the face areas $A_f$ exist for the bookings, and with
the flux dtype of the precision policy; its `F1`, `F2`, `F3` buffers are the totals themselves
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}). The scalar module resets its own register with the FP64 policy
({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}}). The first producer of a stage, the Riemann solve, writes the
total in place through `slot` and names it with `post_slot`
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::slot >}}). A kept part, requested at reset as `"part@dim"`, is a
second tensor of the total's shape that its producer fills ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::kept >}}).

**`add`** adds an increment to some rows of the total
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::add >}}). A contiguous run of rows is one in-place add on a narrow
of the total; any other row list adds row by row. The adds run in call order and are never fused, so successive adds
round as separate in-place additions. A kept part of the same name receives a copy of the increment. The comment at
the add records why it is not an `index_add_`: on CUDA that kernel adds atomically, which for FP64 rows was measured
in the code's own comment at +0.3 ms a step on one deck and +2.9 ms on another
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::add >}}).

**`scale`** multiplies some rows in place by one factor for every row or one factor per row
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::scale >}}). The positivity limiter of @sec-ch08-theta is its
caller.

**`replace`** is the seam writer ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::replace >}}). On the masked faces
it writes either the mean of its own and the peer's values, the same on both sides because the sum commutes, or the
peer's value. It does that for every kept part of the direction and then for the total, through `overwrite_`, under
the amount name `reconcile.x1` for $x_1$[^rg-431e5643024d] or `reconcile.panel` for $x_2$ and $x_3$.

**`overwrite_`** is the one write-and-book ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::overwrite_ >}}).
It takes the new values of a set of faces, or of every face, computes the difference to the values before in the wide
dtype, writes the new values into the total and books @eq-ch10-overwrite. The weights are the face areas laid out
like the written faces, built once per set of faces and device. With a wall batch set, the difference and its
weights go to the batch (@sec-ch10-wallbatch); without one, the rate is booked at the call.

**The written mark.** `add`, `scale` and `overwrite_` set a flag for their direction
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::add >}},
{{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::scale >}},
{{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::overwrite_ >}}), and `apply_prescribed` clears it at its end
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::apply_prescribed >}}). `written_since_prescribed` reads it
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.hpp FluxRegister::written_since_prescribed >}}). `replace` sets it through
`overwrite_`.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_flux_register.<b>` (`add_in_call_order_keeps_the_pin_rounding`) | two adds in order equal the in-place sequence and differ from the fused sum on the chosen operands; the kept part holds the increment | exact (`torch::equal`) | the writer promises the in-place rounding ({{< code tests/test_flux_register.cpp FluxRegister.add_in_call_order_keeps_the_pin_rounding >}}) |
| `test_flux_register.<b>` (`scale_multiplies_the_rows_in_place`) | the scaled rows equal the reference product, other rows are untouched | exact | ({{< code tests/test_flux_register.cpp FluxRegister.scale_multiplies_the_rows_in_place >}}) |
| `test_flux_register.<b>` (`replace_mean_gives_both_sides_the_same_faces`) | both sides of a seam hold the same faces and parts after a mean; other faces and directions are untouched | exact | the mean is symmetric ({{< code tests/test_flux_register.cpp FluxRegister.replace_mean_gives_both_sides_the_same_faces >}}) |
| `test_prescribed_after_sources.<b>` (`the_written_mark_follows_the_writers`) | `add`, `scale` and `replace` set the mark, `apply_prescribed` clears it | pass/fail | ({{< code tests/test_prescribed_after_sources.cpp FluxRegister.the_written_mark_follows_the_writers >}}) |

: Tests of the posts. {#tbl-ch10-posts-tests}

All four pass at the pin, on CPU (@tbl-ch10-ctest-run).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `scale` and the producers' in-place writes book nothing. Only an overwrite is an amount, so a flux a limiter
  withholds is visible in the totals and in the state, not in the monitor's amounts.
:::

1. **Measured costs are the code's comments.** The `index_add_` costs quoted in the Numerical method are
   recorded in a comment at the pin; this chapter did not measure them.
